https://ianslive.in/bulgaria-unknown-dro.text: Bulgaria: Unknown drone explodes near major gas pipeline IANS August 8, 2026 6:41 PM Share on | Sofia, Aug 8 (IANS) Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Saturday confirmed that an unidentified drone exploded not too far from a Trans-Balkan gas pipeline near the former Kardam border checkpoint close to Romania, local media reported. According to Radev, the drone exploded just one kilometre away from a compressor station of the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline, near the former Kardam border checkpoint, after entering Bulgarian Airspace from Romania, Euronews reported. "Noise made by the drone was detected by Romanian border police, and a loud explosion was subsequently heard by the 'General Toshevo' border police patrol," Radev told reporters. He also noted that both Bulgarian and Romanian authorities had failed to detect the drone as it made its way through the airspaces of two countries. He added that increased surveillance operations will be put in place in the region from now on. To identify the type of drone involved in the explosion, an investigation has been launched into the incident. In July, three drones that entered Romanian airspace without authorisation were shot down in three separate incidents. According to the Ministry of National Defence of Romania, the third drone was shot down 12 km northeast of Sulina, within Romania's territorial waters. According to the investigation conducted by the General Prosecutor's Office, one of the drones shot down is of the Shahed type, used by Russia against Ukraine. After the incident, Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) declared a member of the Russian Embassy in Bucharest undesirable (persona non grata) and ordered the member to leave the country. The Foreign Ministry also summoned the Ambassador of Russia to its headquarters upon the instructions of Romanian Foreign Minister Oana-Silvia Toiu. During the meeting, the Romanian side expressed its firm protest against these “illegal and irresponsible” actions and emphasised the clear attribution of responsibility. “The summoning came as a firm response to the repeated violations of Romania’s airspace between 24 and 26 July 2026, during which the Romanian Armed Forces downed three drones that entered national territory without authorisation. https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/black-c.text: This is the first picture of a sex worker brutally murdered in an Oldbury Airbnb by a fanatic of the US show Dexter. Maria Sacaenu was 'lured' to a 'kill room' twisted Benjamin Day had covered with plastic sheeting after becoming obsessed with the Amercian crime series. The 24-year-old, originally from Romania, was contacted on a burner phone by Day, who asked her to meet him in the room he had rented in Barncroft Road, Oldbury, last December. Within 'a very short time of her arrival', forensic student Day had stabbed her to death and started to dismember her body. Day, of Yeadon Close, Redditch, Worcestershire , pleaded not guilty to the murder. But he changed his plea to guilty on the second day of his trial at Wolverhampton Crown Court on Tuesday, October 6. The killer - who was 19 and living with his parents at the time - now faces life behind bars and will be sentenced in December. READ MORE: Dexter copycat killer who tried to mutilate woman in '£30-a-night Oldbury Airbnb kill room' confesses in dramatic court U-turn A post-mortem examination indicated that Ms Sacaenu had been stabbed 78 times by University of Worcester student Day. West Midlands Police said: "The bedroom floor and walls and the bed itself had been lined with plastic sheeting which had been stapled to the wall to secure them. "A canvas knife roll containing multiple knives was discovered as well as a staple gun and duct tape. "Day had also amassed items including an apron, a plastic visor and cleaning materials. "He left the property and flagged down one of our police cars after he had sustained an injury to his hand during the attack, but told he had been attacked by a fox." Day was arrested at Russells Hall Hospital, where he had been taken by paramedics after he dialled 999, at 3.42am on Saturday, December 21. He was initially 'cagey' and 'lied', claiming he had been bitten by a fox or wild dog before later accepting in hospital that his wound was caused by a knife. READ MORE: Unique chance to get BirminghamLive Premium for under 50p a week Detective Inspector Matt Marston, from West Midlands Police's major crime team, led the investigation. He said: "Day had an obsessive personality and had become obsessed with the character Dexter. "He planned this murder in meticulous detail. "It was a pre-planned brutal attack on a defenceless woman lured to the room he had rented. "Day had flagged down officers where he offered them a fabricated story about the reason why he had received an injury to his hand. "Officers were suspicious and he was quickly detained. "The details of this case shocked experienced officers and our thoughts continue to go out to the heartbroken family of Maria at this time." Read more on the case here . Rembrandt's masterpieces become tattoos in the Netherlands Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 29 October 2026 - 14:37 GMT+1 Visitors to the Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, can once again take home a piece of the Dutch master's art, permanently tattooed on their skin. … More The Poor Man's Rembrandt Project , first launched in 2023, has returned by popular demand, bringing tattoo artists into the house where Rembrandt once lived and worked. Among those taking part is Associated Press correspondent Mike Corder , who had covered the original event without imagining he would one day get a tattoo himself. This time, he sat down with renowned Dutch tattoo artist Henk Schiffmacher , better known as Hanky Panky , to have Rembrandt's 1630 etching Self-Portrait with Beret, Wide-Eyed reproduced on his arm. After around half an hour, the young artist's wide-eyed expression was permanently etched into Corder's skin . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Schiffmacher , whose career spans more than 45 years , has tattooed celebrities including Lady Gaga and members of the Red Hot Chili Peppers . He embraces the nickname "Poor Man's Rembrandt" , seeing tattooing as an art form that accompanies its owner for life. The museum's director, Milou Halbesma , says Rembrandt's self-portraits reveal his remarkable honesty , capturing every wrinkle and imperfection, including his own. The project brings together two very different artistic traditions, transforming centuries-old etchings into contemporary body art . As Schiffmacher finished Corder's tattoo, he welcomed him into what he jokingly called the "world of freaks" . The journalist's verdict was simple: happy with the result, if a little sore. The project runs until 7 November .
